A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DYNTS research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original reasoning benchmarks, inference-efficiency measurements, token-selection ablations, and predictor analyses for two models.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds confidence intervals and HumanEval coding results in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The importance predictor, frozen backbone, MSE objective, and question/local/selection-window cache procedure are unchanged. HumanEval uses the existing MATH-trained predictor without introducing a method adaptation.

E1.justification: Appendix D adds HumanEval, extending evaluation into coding beyond the earlier five mathematical benchmarks and GPQA-D scientific question answering. This introduces a distinct task domain while retaining the existing training and evaluation datasets.

E2.justification: The comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged. HumanEval evaluates existing comparators—Transformers, StreamingLLM, SepLLM, H2O, SnapKV, and R-KV—without introducing another comparison method.

E3.justification: Sections 6.1 and Appendix C retain the same models, budgets, sampling settings, training configuration, and evaluation procedures. HumanEval reuses the MATH-trained predictor; no distinct budget, decoding, or scoring protocol is specified.

E4.justification: The new HumanEval experiment explicitly tests whether the mathematical predictor transfers to coding without code fine-tuning. This adds a limited cross-domain generalization analysis; existing component ablations, sensitivity studies, and predictor analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: New Tables 3–4 introduce 95% confidence intervals for accuracy across both models, six benchmarks, and all eight methods. Both versions already report five sampling runs, so this substantially expands uncertainty reporting without establishing additional runs. The interval-estimation procedure is not explained.

E6.justification: Table 5 adds HumanEval scores: DYNTS obtains 88.9 versus Transformers' 89.7 on R1-Qwen and 82.6 versus 83.8 on R1-Llama, alongside existing compression baselines. Tables 3–4 add interval endpoints. Earlier benchmark scores, ablation values, and figure results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, objectives, computational-gain theorem, break-even corollary, and Appendix A proof are unchanged. The new confidence intervals introduce no mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about sparse critical thinking tokens, DYNTS, reasoning accuracy, and efficiency. The added appendix evidence does not redefine the main contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix D newly interprets the confidence intervals as supporting reliable, on-par performance and HumanEval as supporting generalization to other reasoning tasks. Existing mechanism explanations and Appendix E limitations, including possible coding-domain limitations, remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains the same hardware, training sample counts, predictor dimensions, optimizer, batch sizes, and inference details. Code and data access disclosures are unchanged; the HumanEval addition supplies no further implementation instructions.

R1.justification: Related-work discussion and cited-work membership are unchanged. GPQA's reference changes from its 2024 conference entry to the 2023 preprint of the same work, which is a bibliographic update rather than changed research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 corrects the template running header, updates affiliations and publication information, adds acknowledgements and two Appendix D paragraphs, and replaces a results example with a statistical-analysis cross-reference. Most prose and the section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds two confidence-interval tables and one HumanEval table. Existing figures retain their content, with limited repositioning, including Figure 6 moving to page 8, and accompanying text reflow.

improvement.justification: The confidence intervals make uncertainty more visible, and HumanEval adds useful evidence of transfer to coding. These are limited improvements because interval estimation and HumanEval-specific evaluation settings remain undocumented, while overlapping intervals do not establish performance equivalence. The established method and experimental evidence are preserved.
